definitions.explanation: The price at which something was bought, or the price a buyer is willing to pay. Contrasts with {売|う}り{値|ね} (selling price).

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{値|ね}は{五万円|ごまんえん}だった。
{買|か}い{値|ね}より{高|たか}く{売|う}れた。
examples.english: I was able to sell it for more than the purchase price.

examples.japanese: この{株|かぶ}は{買|か}い{値|ね}を{大|おお}きく{下回|したまわ}っている。
examples.english: This stock is well below its purchase price.

notes:
A compound of {買|か}い (buying) + {値|ね} (price). Refers to the price at which something was purchased or the price a buyer offers.

USAGE:
Used in both everyday and financial contexts. In stock and currency markets, {買|か}い{値|ね} is the bid price — the price a buyer is willing to pay.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {買|か}い{値|ね}と{売|う}り{値|ね}: bid and ask prices
- {買|か}い{値|ね}を{下回|したまわ}る: to fall below the purchase price
- {買|か}い{値|ね}がつく: to have a buying price set
- {買|か}い{値|ね}より{高|たか}く{売|う}る: to sell for more than the purchase price

ANTONYM:
{売|う}り{値|ね} (selling price / asking price).
